newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit seen with weak bias ahead of GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit seen with weak bias ahead of GDP data.

text.p: * Ringgit seen weak as dollar/majors has firm tone
* Caution ahead of Malaysia GDP data release
* Activity seen thin before weekend, at month's end
The ringgit was expected to trade with a weak bias as the dollar/majors has a firm tone, dealers said.
Activity was also expected to be thin ahead of the weekend and with most corporate deals settled at the end of the month.
Malaysia's first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data is expected to be released today, though little surprise was anticipated, dealers and analysts said.
The GDP is "expected to be in 7.8-8.2 percent and thus, will leave monetary policy unchanged", said market research firm MMS International.
But any surprises will boost activity. "Some people are expecting it to be below eight percent, and you will see buying of dollars," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
